posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

In Renaissance Europe, science was being transformed into a practice anyone could participate in and even enjoy. The field of astronomy grew rapidly as new instruments were crafted to make discoveries, as you can see on the August page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar. That is when champions like Tycho Brahe, an eccentric man with a metal nose, achieved notoriety by throwing astronomy parties and collecting great volumes of star data that we still use today.

Take a journey through the cosmos with us: Explore the vastness of our Solar System, the Milky Way, and beyond. From the Oort cloud to the Laniakea Supercluster, discover just how tiny we are in the grand scheme of the universe.

Every year, the streets of Yanshui in southern Taiwan erupt into one of the world's most intense fireworks displays.⁠
⁠
The tradition dates back to the 19th century, when villagers prayed to Guan Gong, the Chinese Deity of War, to help end a deadly plague. Firecrackers and fireworks were set off to accompany his procession through the town, and the ritual eventually evolved into the festival seen today.⁠
⁠
Now, thousands of people put on helmets and protective clothing before stepping into a sto

Located near Agadir, Crocoparc Agadir is a botanical garden and conservation center home to over 300 Nile crocodiles, surrounded by more than 300 species of exotic plants, giant cacti, and tropical landscapes.⁠
⁠
Beyond seeing these incredible reptiles up close, visitors can also discover conservation efforts, learn about crocodile breeding, and spot other species like giant tortoises, iguanas, and anacondas.⁠
⁠
📷by: @irfas_scrapbook

After more than 70 years as a symbol of Casablanca’s golden age, a legendary address has a new chapter.⁠
⁠
Royal Mansour Casablanca reopened in 2024 after an eight-year transformation that brought a historic 1950s hotel back to life. ⁠
⁠
The property keeps the spirit of the city’s modernist era while introducing a new vision of Moroccan hospitality.⁠
⁠
By: @royalmansourcollection @royalmansourcasablanca

Florida's spring-fed rivers can look completely covered in duckweed and vegetation from above, but underneath the water runs crystal clear, an must try experience! ⁠
⁠
📷by: @ash_dz

A photographer found and shot every letter of the alphabet in Kuala Lumpur.⁠
⁠
Using Google Maps and weeks of exploring the city, he searched for every letter from A to Z hidden across neighborhoods. Some letters were easy to find, while others took weeks to uncover.⁠
⁠
The result is a collection of 26 photos that show just how differently a city can look from above.⁠
⁠
Which letter is your favorite?⁠
⁠
By: @heartpatrick⁠

Before @lovable.dev existed Nico Wittenberg, a former Google employee spent 14 years thinking about one startup idea before finally building it with Lovable.

After being told the project would require a huge funding round and around 50 engineers, Nico put the idea on hold. Years later, using Lovable, he built AVARA in under a year despite having no engineering background or technical co-founder.

Sala Khao Yai sits on a hilltop in Thailand’s Khao Yai region, where its white buildings and infinity pool follow the natural shape of the land.⁠
⁠
The pool stretches toward the valley, creating the feeling of floating above the mountains, while private villas offer their own rooftop plunge pools and views of the surrounding countryside.⁠
⁠
A stay here starts at around $200 per night, with access to the hilltop infinity pool included.⁠
⁠
By: @sala.khaoyai ⁠

The famous Carreiros do Monte takes you down the streets of Funchal in traditional wicker sledges, a centuries-old tradition where drivers guide wooden baskets downhill using their skill and control. 🛷🌿⁠
⁠
📷 by: @isa__m_

This is one of the most unique coffee experiences in the world.⁠
⁠
In Hanoi, Vietnam, a real railway runs directly through a narrow residential street in the Old Quarter. Over time, small cafés appeared along the tracks, turning everyday life into something truly extraordinary.⁠
⁠
A few times a day, a full-size train slowly passes through the street, with locals and café owners quickly clearing the space just before it arrives. Visitors watch the moment from nearby cafés or designated safe areas

Built in 55 BC, the Theatre of Pompey was ancient Rome's first permanent stone theatre and part of the complex where Julius Caesar was assassinated in 44 BC. ⁠
⁠
Centuries later, its ruins were built over, and today a restaurant sits right inside those 2,000-year-old walls 🏛️🇮🇹. ⁠
⁠
📷 by: @lyracasalenuovo ⁠
Would you add this to your Rome must-visit list?

On Japan’s Tottori Coast, snow, sand dunes, and the sea come together in one rare landscape.⁠
⁠
The famous Tottori Sand Dunes stretch along the Sea of Japan, shaped over thousands of years by wind, waves, and sand carried from nearby rivers. In winter, snow can cover the dunes, creating a rare contrast between white sand, snowy peaks, and the sea.⁠
⁠
Recognized as part of the San’in Kaigan Geopark, this ever-changing coastline shows a different side of Japan’s natural beauty with every season.⁠

Now, a breakthrough in the search for the underlying cause of this condition has come from an unlikely source—a dermatology lab. While investigating why autoimmune diseases are more common in women, scientists identified a potential genetic driver behind preeclampsia, offering an explanation that could point the way to a cure.

No bigger than my thumb, the handfish takes an entire year to cover a distance equivalent to that of a standard basketball court. A humpback cow and calf are joined by two males in the Cook Islands and photographed by @brianskerry. Males escort females with calves in hopes that they will be the next ones to mate with the mothers. Calves emit soft, whisper-like squeaks while adult males sing in low, guttural moans and high-pitched whoops and screeches.
